name: Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Ltd. (Foxconn)
monetization: World's largest AI-server assembler — builds Nvidia rack systems and Stargate/US AI-infrastructure hardware; cloud & networking passed 51% of revenue in Q2 2026.
description_md: Hon Hai (Foxconn) is the world's largest electronics contract manufacturer and, since the AI buildout, the largest assembler of AI servers — building Nvidia GB/VR-generation rack systems for hyperscalers and neoclouds. In Q2 2026 its cloud-and-networking segment (housing AI servers) exceeded 51% of total revenue for the first time, surpassing the consumer-electronics (iPhone) business that defined the company for two decades. It is expanding US production, including Houston facilities tied to AI-server programs (Apple server assembly; reported Stargate-related hardware work with OpenAI), and struck a November 2025 partnership with OpenAI on next-generation AI infrastructure hardware.
ai_monetization_md: Assembly and integration revenue on AI racks: Q2 2026 revenue was ~$78.7B (+39.8% y/y) with record Q2 net profit of NT$59.97B (~$1.86B, +35% y/y) — profit growing far slower than revenue because assembly margins are thin and the GPU content passes through. The OpenAI partnership covers jointly developing and US-manufacturing AI data-center hardware; notably, **OpenAI made no purchase commitment**, so the arrangement is capability positioning rather than backlog. Foxconn Industrial Internet (the listed China subsidiary) nearly doubled H1 profit on AI-server orders.
ai_strategy_md: Convert consumer-electronics scale into AI-infrastructure scale: dedicate capacity to Nvidia rack systems ahead of demand, localize US manufacturing (Houston, Texas; Wisconsin) to capture sovereign/onshoring requirements including Stargate-linked work, and move up the value chain from boards to full data-center integration (liquid cooling, power shelves) — while management flags upstream CoWoS packaging, not orders, as the 2027 growth ceiling.
risk_notes_md: **Margin structure:** assembly economics mean Foxconn books enormous revenue on AI servers but captures a thin slice — profit +35% on revenue +40% in Q2 2026; a mix shift alone cannot re-rate margins. **No-commitment partnerships:** the OpenAI deal carries no purchase obligation — capacity built for it is at Foxconn's risk if Stargate deployment slips. **Concentration:** deeply tied to the Nvidia ecosystem and a few hyperscaler/neocloud programs; some reported figures (Houston/Stargate scope) remain unverified in detail. **Geopolitics:** Taiwan-China exposure plus US onshoring costs.

observations.notes: +39.8% y/y, driven by cloud and AI-server revenue; converted from NT$ (company monthly disclosures).

events.title: OpenAI partnership on US-built AI data-center hardware — with no purchase commitment
events.why_it_matters: OpenAI gets US manufacturing capacity and design input on next-gen racks without committing dollars; Foxconn carries the capacity risk. A textbook example of headline partnership ≠ contracted revenue.

events.title: Q2 2026: record profit; AI servers >51% of revenue; CEO names CoWoS as 2027 ceiling
events.why_it_matters: The revenue-mix crossover makes Foxconn an AI-infrastructure company by composition; management explicitly located the binding constraint upstream in TSMC packaging, not in demand.
